title: Closed support as a relative section complex
statement:
Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion,
with complementary open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow T$.
For a complex $K$ of etale $A$-module sheaves,
there is a natural isomorphism of ordinary derived
$A$-module complexes

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*A_D,K)
\cong\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(R\Gamma(T,K)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma(V,v^*K)\bigr)[-1].
$$

proof.text: Prove naturality of globalSectionsUpperStarMap directly from the adjunction unit and terminal-section identifications, and apply NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex to obtain q with its required component formula. Apply [new-lem-amb-closed-support-hom-sequence] to get a natural underived kernel arrow alpha and short exactness on injective sheaves.

Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to form the functorial resolution I=R(K). Map alpha termwise. The preceding short exact sequences in every degree give a short exact sequence of complexes C -> E -> B. Define the map C -> Cone(q)[-1] explicitly by inclusion in the shifted source summand. Identify it with the existing kernel comparison [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] via the unique isomorphism from the kernel object; hence it is a quasi-isomorphism. Its naturality is the mappingCone.map formula on this summand.

Use the already proved Functor.rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso of WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.KInjective to identify RF(QK) with Q(F(I)). Its naturality follows by composing the quotientCompQhIso naturalities and inverse naturality of the derived-functor unit. Compose with Q of the explicit quasi-isomorphism and Q.commShiftIso(-1). Naturality of the resolution, of the cone inclusion, and of the shift comparison gives exactly the required equation. No separate identification of the open term as a derived functor is needed by this concrete statement.
